newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Sun could ship JavaStation with drive.
newsitem.headline: Sun could ship JavaStation with drive.

text.p: Sun Microsystems Inc could in the future ship a version of its JavaStation network computer, launched last week, with a hard disk drive, Ed Zanter, President of Sun Microsystems Computer Co said on Thursday.

"In a short time it will have flash RAM capability and just-in-time chipset compilers...there is an opportunity longer term to see if we can put in a hard disk," Zanter told a news conference alongside a three-day seminar to present Sun and the Java programming language and applications to European company information technology managers.
Sun's JavaStation, one of several NCs being brought out by various companies, was unveiled last week as a direct challenge to the desktop personal computer (PC) found in most businesses.

With no hard, floppy or CD-ROM disk drives for storage, but just a microprocessor and limited memory, a network computer (NC) uses Internet technology to pull programmes and information, as and when needed, off a company's central server.
Because of this a JavaStation, priced at under $1,000, would cost companies around $2,500 a year to run and maintain, compared with around $12,500 for a traditional network-based PC, Zanter said.
Product line manager Charles Tierney said there were some applications where a disk drive's higher storage capacity could prove advantageous, such as an information kiosk in a shopping mall.
"At night information could be downloaded from a central location, filling the disk with video. When it is updated the next night, the information would be replaced," he said.
Zanter said immediate feedback from companies after the JavaStation launch went against making the machine more complex. "They are telling us keep it simple," he said.
